teacher_notes: Good place to distinguish the value of a limit from the value of the function at the point.
explanation: Direct substitution gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}$, so factor first: $\frac{x^2-9}{x-3}=\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3}=x+3$ for $x\neq3$. The limit is therefore $3+3=6$. The function has a removable discontinuity at $x=3$, so the limit exists even though the function is undefined there.
